inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 7: 233.11m weighted basic + 2.09m dilutive options/restricted stock + 0.57m unvested restricted/deferred stock = 235.8m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 21.17m convertible-note conversion shares are EXCLUDED and all three convertible issues ($3.5bn principal) are carried as debt at par: the 2030 ($192.29) and 2031 ($224.93) conversion prices are out of the money, and the 2029 notes ($108.39 conversion price, 9.23m shares) are worth par, not shares, at any value per share below $108.39, which is where every scenario lands. At the market price the 2029 notes would convert (+3.9% dilution, -$1.0bn debt).
inputs.cash_note: ESTIMATE of free cash, not balance-sheet cash. Balance sheet at 2026-09-30: cash $8,257.5m + short-term investments $69.1m. Of that, $2.7bn is ticketing client cash owed to venues/clients, and event-related deferred revenue ($4.41bn total deferred revenue) net of event-related prepaids and artist accruals is fan money held against future shows. The company's own 'free cash' definition (10-Q liquidity section) nets these; the 10-Q does not print the figure, so $1.5bn is estimated (5.56bn ex-client cash - ~3.95bn event deferred revenue - ~1.6bn artist accruals/cash collected for others + ~1.5bn event prepaids) plus $69m short-term investments. +/-$500m on this estimate is +/-$2.1 per share.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation expense $155.2m (LYV_Annual_FY2025.txt:2966) + taxes paid for net share settlement of equity awards $126.7m (line 2998). Live Nation publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule; the withholding outflow is large because awards vest well above grant-date value.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.3 = cost of equity ~10.8%; pre-tax cost of debt 4.3% (10-Q weighted average, convert-heavy), ~3.3% after tax; ~80/20 equity/debt at market gives ~9.3%, rounded to 9.0% because the value-based capital structure is more debt-heavy than the market-based one. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows and the weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already an operating expense inside AOI, so no lease adjustment is made and the $2.16bn operating lease liability is excluded from net debt (treatment B by construction).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests ($194.8m FY2025, $234.8m FY2024; distributions to NCI ~$250m/yr) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-and-leakage rate: ~26% cash tax on EBIT then ~24% of NOPAT to minorities = 44%. Redeemable NCI ($1,147m) and NCI ($731m) are therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT on this basis $1,227m x 0.56 = $687m, less after-tax net interest (~$125m) and the excess of actual over normalised acquisition expense (~$97m) = ~$465m against reported attributable net income of $496m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical/consumer; adaptations file read for NCI, float and leases). Live Nation is a promoter/venue operator/ticketer, not a financial or property vehicle. FCF BASE: trailing reported FCF is not used as the base. OCF swings by more than $1bn a year on client cash and event deferred revenue (9M-2026 OCF $2.1bn includes a $2.75bn accrued-expense build), and GAAP operating income is distorted by one-offs (FY2024 Astroworld $455m; 9M-2026 $450m DOJ/states litigation reserve, which is the whole of the 25% fall in 9M GAAP operating income; ex-reserve it rose 7%). The base is built from AOI. EBITDA MARGIN DEFINITION: AOI (pre-SBC) minus amortisation of non-recoupable ticketing contract advances (~$88m, a real cash payment to clients that AOI adds back) minus normalised acquisition expenses (~$135m; FY2025 $260m, FY2024 $129m, includes merger-related legal cost) plus interest earned on the fan/client float (~$85m, 0.3% of revenue, against ~$150m total interest income; the float itself is netted out of cash, so its income belongs in the flows under the matching-asset rule). FY2026: AOI ~$2,568m (guidance: high-single-digit growth; 9M AOI $2,367m, +9%) on ~$28.5bn revenue = 9.0% AOI margin, 8.5% on this definition. CAPEX: full capex is charged, including revenue-generating venue capex (FY2025 $1,062m; FY2026 guide ~$1.1bn gross, ~85% revenue-generating); the growth and margin paths are the return on it. Acquisitions ($572m in 9M-2026) and NCI buy-ins ($884m FY2025) are not modelled, so growth is organic only. TIMING: FY0 = FY2025 actuals, year 1 = FY2026 (guidance year, nine months reported), discounted a full year against a 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet; this is the house convention and is modestly conservative. LEGAL: the $450m litigation reserve accrued in 2026 and unpaid is deducted in the equity bridge; structural remedies sit in the bear scenario. BUYBACKS: none of substance ($23.5m FY2025, no program); the flat count is a modelling convention funded only through net-share settlement ($126.7m). Not included (conservative): investments in nonconsolidated affiliates. SBC 9M-2026 $142.2m (+12%), net-share-settlement taxes $109.0m.

equity_bridge.item: Governmental investigations and litigation reserve (accrued, unpaid)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 6: $450m recognised in 9M-2026 for the Settling States and the jury damages award; not tax-effected

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue (FY2019-FY2025 CAGR 13.9%, FY2022-FY2025 14.7%), tempered to organic growth ex-acquisitions
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful. Total equity was negative in FY2020-FY2021 and is $0.9bn against $25bn revenue; EPS to common is distorted by redeemable-NCI accretion (FY2025 -$0.24 on $691m net income); owner FCF went from $1,301m (FY2022) to $52m (FY2025) on float timing and a tripling of capex. Revenue is the only usable series, so the house default (equity CAGR) cannot be applied.
historical_growth.notes: revenue_5yr_cagr is FY2019-FY2025 (six years) because FY2020 was a COVID shutdown year ($1.9bn). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - net-share-settlement taxes): FY2022 1,301; FY2023 799; FY2024 908; FY2025 52. Reported FCF fell 78% over FY2022-FY2025 while AOI rose 69%: capex rose from $347m to $1,062m and SBC plus settlement taxes from $187m to $282m.

base.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined cash tax (~26% of EBIT; FY2025 cash taxes $313m) and NCI leakage (~24% of NOPAT). See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_note: Deferred revenue grows with sales (+$342m FY2025) but is offset by receivables, artist advances and prepaids; three-year net working-capital change shows no reliable positive capture.
base.narrative: Venue build-out earns its keep; DOJ settlement terms hold.

bull.cash_tax_rate_note: NCI leakage drifts down as minorities are bought in.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands on guidance (revenue +13%, AOI up high single digits, ~180m fans). After that fan growth runs mid-single digit, led by international stadium and arena shows, with pricing and onsite spend adding 2-3 points; revenue growth fades from 8% to 3.5%. The venue programme (Venue Nation, ~$0.9bn a year of revenue-generating capex) lifts the mix toward operated-venue and sponsorship income, taking the margin (AOI less non-recoupable advances and acquisition costs, plus float interest) from 8.5% to 9.3%, an incremental pre-tax return of roughly 20% on the growth capex. The DOJ settlement is approved broadly as filed: the 15% amphitheater fee cap, 13 venues losing exclusive booking and third-party access to Ticketmaster cost ticketing growth but not its franchise, and the states' remedies phase adds money, not a break-up. Capex intensity falls from 3.8% to 2.2% of revenue as the build-out matures. Tax plus minority leakage stays at 44% of EBIT.
scenario_narratives.bull: International fan growth stays in the teens for several years and the new arenas and amphitheaters fill, so operated-venue economics (concessions, premium seating, parking) and sponsorship (64% AOI margin, growing mid-teens) become a larger share of profit and the margin reaches 10.5%. Ticketmaster keeps share despite platform opening because content, not exclusivity, drives client choice; the verdict is narrowed on appeal. Buying in minorities trims NCI leakage to 40%, and deferred revenue growth runs ahead of artist advances (3% working-capital capture). This case needs the venue returns, the legal outcome and the consumer all to cooperate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The remedies phase in the Litigating States case, or rejection of the DOJ settlement under the Tunney Act, produces structural relief: Ticketmaster loses exclusivity more broadly or is separated from promotion, and the FTC drip-pricing case caps fees. Ticketing AOI ($1.13bn, 37% margin, nearly half of segment profit) falls by about a quarter, taking a point off the consolidated margin, while a consumer slowdown and a thin stadium slate in 2027-2028 cut growth to 2-4% just as the venue capex comes on line with lower utilisation. Margin settles at 7.5%, capex stays at 2.5% of revenue to maintain a larger venue estate, and with $9.8bn of debt most of the enterprise value belongs to lenders. Any penalty beyond the $450m reserve would come off this value dollar for dollar.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a jury has found monopoly liability, the states' remedies phase and Tunney Act approval are open, the FTC case survived a motion to dismiss, and net debt is ~3.2x AOI, so a single regulator can impair equity disproportionately. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance and nine months of results support it. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs venue returns, a benign legal outcome and sustained consumer demand at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Live Nation is valued on what an owner keeps: AOI after the cash costs it adds back (stock compensation and net-share-settlement taxes, non-recoupable ticketing advances, acquisition costs), after cash tax, after the minorities' share, and after all capex including the venue build-out. On that basis FY2026 owner FCF is roughly $0.4-0.5bn against AOI of ~$2.6bn, and the gap is the finding. The market price capitalises AOI at ~20x EV and treats growth capex, SBC and minority distributions as below the line; this model does not. The equity is a residual after ~$8.3bn of net debt, so small changes in enterprise value move value per share by multiples.
key_risks_to_valuation: Free cash is estimated at $1.5bn; the 10-Q does not print it. Each $500m is $2.1 per share.
Leverage: net debt plus the legal reserve is roughly half of base enterprise value, so a 10% change in EV moves value per share by about 20%.
Terminal capex intensity (2.2% of revenue base) is a judgment; maintenance capex as the company defines it is only ~0.5% of revenue, depreciation ~1.6%. At 1.7% the base value rises materially.
NCI leakage is modelled as a fixed share of NOPAT; continued buy-ins would lower it but cost cash that is not modelled.
Legal outcome is binary in parts: structural separation of Ticketmaster is in the bear case only at a 25% weight.
Year 1 is FY2026 discounted a full year although ten and a half months have elapsed: conservative by a few percent of EV.
